mainTopic: רב פפא's questions about יד (an incomplete statement that hints at a full one) in קידושין and in פאה
overview: The גמרא continues discussing ידות, incomplete statements that point to a full statement. רב פפא asks whether יד works for קידושין. The case is a man who betroths one woman and then says to another woman only 'and you.' That could mean 'you too' or 'you, watch.' The גמרא challenges whether רב פפא could really have been unsure, since elsewhere he seems to accept יד for קידושין. It answers that there he was only asking about שמואל's view. רב פפא then asks the same question about פאה, where someone said 'and this' about a second furrow without saying 'too.' Along the way the גמרא learns, and proves from a ברייתא, that a person may make his entire field פאה. Finally it lays out both sides of רב פפא's question: does פאה's comparison to קרבנות give it יד, or does that comparison teach only the rule of בל תאחר? The גמרא then begins to quote the ברייתא that is the source of the comparison, and that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רב פפא asks: does an incomplete statement work for betrothal?
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא asks whether יד, an incomplete statement, works for קידושין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא asked: Does an incomplete statement work for betrothal, or not?
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא raises a question: can קידושין take effect through a יד, a partial statement that only hints at the full meaning?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now the topic was ידות in נדרים. רב פפא now asks whether the same idea applies to קידושין. The question opens a new branch of discussion.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked, or raised a question he was unsure about
'Handle': an incomplete statement that hints at a full one
Betrothal, the first stage of marriage

phrases.english: Rav Pappa asked:
Is there a 'handle' for betrothal, or not?
phrases.notes: A 'handle' is a half-said statement that still clearly carries the full meaning.

steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether an incomplete statement can create קידושין.

steps.title: What is the case? The obvious version is rejected
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the exact case. It rejects a case where he said 'and you too,' because that is clearly full קידושין.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? If you say he told one woman 'You are betrothed to me' and told her friend 'And you too,' that is obviously real betrothal!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the case is. It tries one version and throws it out because that version is too obvious to need asking.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'and you too' clearly carry over the full betrothal statement. That counts as complete קידושין, not a doubtful יד. So רב פפא must have meant a different case.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? How does it look?

phrases.english: What is the case?
If you say that he said to a woman
'You are hereby betrothed to me,'
and he said to her friend, 'And you too' —
it is obvious: that is betrothal itself!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the case behind the question in step 1.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact case of רב פפא's question.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proposed case, not the question itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: 'And you too' is a full statement, so there is nothing to ask.

steps.title: The real case: he said only 'and you'
steps.stepSummary: The real question is a case where he said just 'and you.' That could mean 'you too' or 'you, watch.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the case is where he told one woman 'You are betrothed to me' and told her friend just 'And you.' Do we say he meant 'And you too,' so the betrothal works on the friend? Or maybe he meant 'And you, see this,' so the betrothal does not work on the friend?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the real case. He left out the word 'too,' so his words to the second woman are unclear.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without 'too,' 'and you' could continue the betrothal, which would make it a יד. It could also just be telling her to watch, as a witness. The doubt is whether such an unclear hint is enough to create קידושין.

phrases.english: Rather, it is a case where he said to a woman
'You are hereby betrothed to me,'
and he said to her friend, 'And you.'

phrases.aramaic: מִי אָמְרִינַן ״וְאַתְּ נָמֵי״ אֲמַר לַהּ לַחֲבֶירְתָּהּ,
phrases.english: Do we say that he told her friend 'And you too,'
and the betrothal takes effect on the friend,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִּלְמָא: ״וְאַתְּ חֲזַאי״ אֲמַר לַהּ לַחֲבֶירְתַּהּ,
phrases.english: or perhaps he told her friend 'And you, see,'
phrases.notes: He would mean: 'and you, watch me betroth this woman.'

phrases.english: and the betrothal does not take effect on the friend?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected case from step 2 with the real one.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The case is where he said only 'and you,' which is unclear.
steps.whatToRemember: The question about יד in קידושין is about 'and you' without 'too.' It could mean 'you too' or 'you, watch.'

steps.title: Challenge: רב פפא elsewhere seems to accept a 'handle' for betrothal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: elsewhere רב פפא asked אביי whether שמואל accepts unclear ידות. That implies רב פפא himself accepts clear ידות in קידושין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Was רב פפא really unsure about this? But רב פפא asked אביי, 'Does שמואל hold that unclear handles count as handles?' This shows that רב פפא holds there is a handle for betrothal!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the idea that רב פפא was unsure. Another statement of his seems to show he already accepted יד for קידושין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא was only puzzled about unclear ידות. That suggests he took for granted that clear ידות work in קידושין. If so, why would he ask about יד in קידושין here?

keyTerms.meaning: Unclear handles: hints that do not clearly show the meaning

phrases.english: And was Rav Pappa really unsure?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא מִדַּאֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב פָּפָּא לְאַבָּיֵי:
phrases.english: But from the fact that Rav Pappa said to Abaye:
'Does Shmuel hold
that unclear handles count as handles?'
it follows that Rav Pappa holds
that there is a handle for betrothal!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions whether the dilemma in steps 1-3 could be real.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רב פפא was unsure whether יד works for קידושין.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Asking only about unclear ידות implies he already accepted clear ידות in קידושין.

steps.title: Answer: he was only asking about שמואל's view
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא was asking about one point inside שמואל's opinion. That does not show his own view.
steps.simpleTranslation: He was asking אביי about one part of what שמואל holds.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. In that conversation, רב פפא was only discussing שמואל's opinion, not giving his own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל held that even unclear ידות work for קידושין. רב פפא questioned that one point within שמואל's opinion. He did not mean that he himself agrees that clear ידות work, so his own question here stays open.

keyTerms.meaning: One thing out of, one point within

phrases.aramaic: חֲדָא מִגּוֹ מַאי דִּסְבִירָא לֵיהּ לִשְׁמוּאֵל
phrases.english: One point from among what Shmuel holds
he said to Abaye.

steps.triggerLanguage: חֲדָא מִגּוֹ מַאי דִּסְבִירָא לֵיהּ לִשְׁמוּאֵל
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the source: a question asked within someone else's view.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב פפא's question to אביי showed his own view that יד works for קידושין.
steps.terutzMaskana: He was only probing שמואל's opinion, so his own doubt remains.
steps.confusionAlert: Asking 'does שמואל hold X?' does not mean the one asking agrees with the rest of שמואל's view.
steps.whatToRemember: רב פפא's question about יד in קידושין stands. His talk with אביי was only about שמואל's opinion.

steps.title: רב פפא asks: does a 'handle' work for פאה?
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא asks whether יד works for פאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא asked: Is there a handle for פאה, or is there no handle for פאה?
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא raises a new question: can a partial statement designate produce as פאה?
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same kind of question as before, now applied to פאה. That is the corner of the field left for the poor. A new branch opens.

keyTerms.meaning: The corner of the field left for the poor

phrases.english: Rav Pappa asked:

phrases.aramaic: יֵשׁ יָד לְפֵאָה, אוֹ אֵין יָד לְפֵאָה?
phrases.english: Is there a handle for pe'ah, or is there no handle for pe'ah?

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֵי רַב פָּפָּא יֵשׁ יָד לְפֵאָה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether an incomplete statement can designate פאה.

steps.title: What is the case? 'And this too' is obviously full פאה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects a case where he said 'this furrow is פאה, and this one too,' because that is clearly real פאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? If you say he said 'This furrow shall be פאה, and this one too,' that is complete פאה.
steps.whatsHappening: Just as with קידושין, the גמרא asks what the case is. It rejects the version that is too obvious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'too' clearly carries over the declaration of פאה to the second furrow. So it is a full declaration, not a doubtful יד.

keyTerms.meaning: A furrow or row in a field

phrases.english: What is the case?
If you say he said, 'This furrow shall be pe'ah,
and this one too' —
that is complete pe'ah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the case for the question in step 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact case of the פאה question.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: 'And this too' is a full declaration.

steps.title: The real case: he said 'and this' without 'too'
steps.stepSummary: The question is about someone who said 'and this' without 'too.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The question is about a case where he said 'and this' and did not say 'too.' What is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the real case of the פאה question. The second furrow was mentioned without the word 'too.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without 'too,' 'and this' could mean the second furrow is also פאה. It could also mean the opposite, that this furrow stays his. That makes it an unclear יד.

keyTerms.meaning: When he asked, the case he was asking about

phrases.english: When he asked,
it was a case where he said 'and this'
and did not say 'too.' What is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected case from step 7.

steps.title: Inference: can a whole field be declared פאה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא infers from רב פפא's question that a person can declare an entire field פאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does this show that if he said 'The whole field shall be פאה,' it becomes פאה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses to draw a side point from רב פפא's question. It asks whether we learn that a whole field can be made פאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first furrow alone must already be enough פאה for the field. Otherwise, adding a second furrow would obviously mean 'also.' If רב פפא still thinks the second furrow might become פאה, then a person can give more than the required amount, even the whole field.

phrases.english: Does it follow that when he said
'The entire field shall be pe'ah,'
it becomes pe'ah?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכְּלָל דְּכִי אָמַר שָׂדֶה כּוּלָּהּ תֶּיהְוֵי פֵּאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a side conclusion from the case defined in step 8.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רב פפא's question shows that one can designate an entire field as פאה.
steps.whyThisMatters: It raises the question of whether פאה has an upper limit, or whether one may give even the whole field.

steps.title: Yes, a whole field can be made פאה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא agrees that a person can make his entire field פאה, and proves it from a ברייתא that reads the words 'פאת שדך'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, it is true. A ברייתא teaches: How do we know that if a person wants to make his whole field פאה, he may do it? The פסוק says, 'the corner of your field.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the inference from Step 9 with 'yes'. It backs this up with a ברייתא saying a person may make his whole field פאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 9 inferred from רב פפא's question that even a whole field can be פאה. Here the גמרא confirms that this is not a new idea, because a ברייתא already says it. The ברייתא reads 'פאת שדך' to mean that 'your field' itself can be the corner.

keyTerms.meaning: And so it was taught in a ברייתא (here it brings support, not an attack)

steps.confusionAlert: Usually 'וְהָתַנְיָא' opens a challenge. Here it comes right after 'אין' (yes), so it brings support.

phrases.english: Yes, and so it is taught in a ברייתא:
From where do we know that if one wants
to make his entire field פאה,
he may do so?
The verse says: "the corner of your field."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 19:9. The idea is that the whole 'field' can be the 'corner'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Confirms the inference made in Step 9 and supports it with a ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes. A ברייתא based on 'פאת שדך' teaches that a whole field may be made פאה.

steps.title: The two sides of רב פפא's question
steps.stepSummary: Does פאה work with יד because it is compared to קרבנות? Or is that comparison only for the rule of בל תאחר?
steps.simpleTranslation: Do we say that since פאה is compared to קרבנות, it works like them? קרבנות work with יד, so פאה should too. Or maybe the comparison teaches only that you may not delay giving פאה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to רב פפא's question and spells out both sides of it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Side one says that the Torah compares פאה to קרבנות, so everything true of קרבנות, including יד, applies to פאה. Side two says the comparison has a narrow purpose: you may not delay giving פאה, just as you may not delay bringing a קרבן. If side two is right, the comparison tells us nothing about יד.

keyTerms.meaning: It was compared or linked (by a Torah הֶקֵּשׁ)
Just as ... so too (the form of a comparison)
The ban on delaying a promised gift or offering

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that a comparison in the Torah can be read broadly or narrowly. The whole question turns on how far the comparison reaches.

phrases.english: Do we say:
since it is compared to offerings,
just as offerings have יד,
so too פאה has יד.
Or perhaps:
when it was compared,
it was compared only for "do not delay."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side point about a whole field and goes back to רב פפא's main question from Step 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the comparison of פאה to קרבנות make יד work for פאה, or does it teach only בל תאחר?

steps.title: Where is פאה compared to קרבנות?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where the Torah compares פאה to קרבנות and starts to bring a ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where is this comparison found? As a ברייתא teaches:
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא asks for the source of the comparison and opens a ברייתא that will be quoted next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 11 relied on a comparison between פאה and קרבנות but did not show where it comes from. Here the גמרא stops to find that source before going on.

keyTerms.meaning: A Torah link between two topics placed together
As it was taught (brings in a ברייתא as the source)

phrases.english: And where is it compared?
As it is taught in a ברייתא:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the comparison that Step 11 relied on.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The Torah source that compares פאה to קרבנות.
